nTop · Jet20 engineering · Closure preparation

From open requirements
to release evidence

What blocks the engine, what can advance now, and what must be demonstrated.

09 SEP 2026C5 PLAN / C5 REQUIREMENTS / R2 NATIVE EVIDENCEPREPARED FOR ENGINEERING REVIEW

The model now passes its recorded geometry and software criteria. The remaining requirements concern the physical engine and its production definition.

All 26 hardware requirements remain blocked by missing definitions or accepted evidence.

This package prepares the work needed to close them. It adds a complete action matrix, component and joint worksheets, and a source-linked load handoff.

No hardware requirement is closed by this preparation. Some need released documents or inspections; others require analysis, demonstrations, or tests.

Requirements and verification · Actual engine in 3D · SysML v2 model

01Start with the inputs that control the design

The SAR mission, 10800-second continuous duty and total life, and production preferences are now defined. The user confirms approximately 110 kg total takeoff mass. C5 assigns fuel, running-time and interface assumptions to all 18 planning decisions. These assumptions require physical validation. Open the current duty and production study.

1. Validate the assumed duty and interfacesUse the C5 planning basis. Replace its reference-flow, fuel, life and interface assumptions with aircraft, component and test evidence.
2. Establish component evidence and physical limitsObtain applicable maps. Select materials and bearings. Resolve thermal, structural, clearance, pressure, and control limits.
3. Complete the production definitionRelease actual part numbers, drawings, joints, seals, wiring, inspection plans, and assembly instructions. Review access with actual tools.
4. Release each test, then collect evidenceApprove test-specific entry criteria before each component or engine test. Correlate the model and complete the applicable durability and installation demonstrations.

This is a proposed dependency sequence, not a calendar or an approved test procedure. Component tests and design work can proceed iteratively. Test release precedes the test it authorizes.

J20-MIS-001Blocked

Installed design-point thrust

Current evidence: A normalized 20 lbf solution exists; installed thrust has not been measured.

Next work: Define the thrust balance boundary, load-cell calibration, installation corrections, and uncertainty budget.

Closure evidence: A calibrated installed-equivalent thrust report tied to engine configuration and the agreed duty.

Method: test. Owner role: Responsible engine engineer. Decisions: D01, D02, D03.

Exact current acceptance criterion

Calibrated installed-equivalent test demonstrates at least 88.96443230521 N after agreed uncertainty and installation corrections. Reference-normalized predictions cannot close this requirement.

J20-MIS-002Blocked

SAR duty and flight envelope

Current evidence: The user confirms an expendable SAR drone and 10800 seconds of mission duty. C4 assumes a reference-hold schedule, contingency and ground allowances; a validated flight trajectory is absent.

Next work: Replace the C4 reference-hold proxy with an aircraft-based altitude, Mach, thrust, temperature and transient matrix, then verify the required points.

Closure evidence: A reviewed envelope matrix and applicable test evidence for every required point.

Method: test. Owner role: Responsible engine engineer. Decisions: D01, D03.

Exact current acceptance criterion

Demonstrate 10800 seconds of continuous operation on the approved SAR operating schedule. Define the altitude/Mach thrust schedule; 20 lbf across every envelope point is not yet specified. Account for factory/preflight running separately from the 10800-second total service-life requirement.

J20-FUE-001Blocked

Fuel compatibility

Current evidence: C4 selects Jet A-1 as the assumed design grade and Jet A as a separately qualified alternate. Bearing lubrication and complete-system compatibility remain unverified.

Next work: Verify the selected fuel basis with a wetted-material compatibility matrix. Obtain bearing lubrication requirements before accepting the current fuel-fed service concept.

Closure evidence: Fuel-specific compatibility and combustion evidence for the complete pump, injector, hose, seal, and lubricant system.

Method: test. Owner role: Responsible engine engineer. Decisions: D04.

Exact current acceptance criterion

Select a fuel grade and demonstrate combustion, seal, hose, pump, injector, and lubricant compatibility. Jet A and Jet A-1 are proposed interpretations of normal jet fuel; no grade compatibility is accepted without evidence.

Compare flow, speed, fuel, station pressure/temperature, and thrust against withheld measured points using an approved uncertainty and error budget.

Current evidence: The user revises total takeoff mass to approximately 110 kg and targets L/D approximately 12. C5 retains the fuel/tank and service assumptions. The exact L/D-12 force screen has a small thrust deficit; actual drag, mass/CG and tank fit remain unverified.

Next work: Verify the revised aircraft drag polar and installed thrust at the reference point. Resolve the small nominal force deficit with actual mass, aerodynamic performance or verified thrust; then complete fuel, CG, mount and service integration.

Closure evidence: An accepted interface definition and inspection/test evidence for mounts, envelope, inlet, exhaust, fuel, and electrical supply.

Method: inspection and test. Owner role: Responsible engine engineer. Decisions: D02, D15, D17.

Exact current acceptance criterion

Define mount loads, mass/envelope limits, inlet recovery/distortion, exhaust losses, fuel supply, and electrical supply at stated boundaries. For the expendable SAR vehicle, define the mission-end propulsion shutdown interface and vehicle-level termination or recovery plan. Acceptance of vehicle loss does not demonstrate acceptable ground impact risk. Use the confirmed approximately 110 kg total takeoff mass, including fuel and payload. Demonstrate the installed thrust/drag balance and fuel mass, volume and CG integration. C5 budget allocations are assumed inputs, not aircraft evidence. Treat L/D approximately 12 as the aircraft design target at 3048 m, Mach 0.5, ISA. Verify the actual thrust/drag balance; the approximate target does not permit negative thrust margin. No actual L/D is verified by the requirement.

Record this deviation from the confirmed 10800-second life and qualify the longer provision before use; it is not accepted hardware evidence.

03Prepared manufacturing and evidence files

The component worksheet has one row for each of the 71 native groups. Each row records its source mesh hash, original-mesh bounds, function, joints, and missing production fields.

Native groups can contain several physical pieces. They must be split into actual made and purchased part numbers. Original-mesh bounds are packaging references, not tolerance or fit definitions.

The joint worksheet covers all 23 scheduled joints. It retains nominal sizes, counts, holes, positions, and stack dimensions. Thread class, preload, locking, seals, and production instructions remain empty.

  • All 26 closure actions (CSV)
  • 71 native group definitions (CSV)
  • 23 joint definitions (CSV)
  • Conditional load and bearing handoff (JSON)
  • Verification record template (JSON)
  • Closure plan and source hashes (JSON)

These are generated starting templates. Copy them to working records before filling them. Regeneration replaces the templates. Blank CSV cells and JSON null values mean undefined. They do not mean zero or not applicable.

The verification record template captures the tested article, configuration, procedure, criteria, calibration, raw data, uncertainty, deviations, and responsible review. A completed record still needs requirement-specific assessment.

04Conditional load and bearing handoff

The following ranges are derived from 43 numerically matched cases within the retained study limits. The study attempted 54 cases; 11 failed numerically. These failures do not define an idle or stability boundary.

Conditional metricMinimumMaximumSource point indices, zero-based
Shaft speed [rpm]5885810000042 / 53
Shaft torque [N m]0.8865284.1610742 / 17
Nominal shaft torsion [MPa]8.8184541.390942 / 17
Case pressure difference screen [Pa]39863.821269842 / 17
Case membrane hoop stress screen [MPa]1.9890410.612842 / 17
Impeller tip acceleration [m/s2]1.51643e+064.37737e+0642 / 53
Turbine tip acceleration [m/s2]1.50722e+064.35078e+0642 / 53
Applicability

The reference model is normalized to the sizing duty. These values are conditional design inputs. They exclude transient, fault, overspeed, installation, and qualification load cases.

The shaft stress screen assumes a uniform solid 8 mm shaft. The case stress screen treats a thin cylinder under compressor total-pressure difference. Both omit detailed features, combined loads, thermal gradients, fatigue, and material allowables.

The nominal cold turbine radial gap is 0.300 mm (model input). Required running clearance, tolerances, runout, bearing motion, and differential growth must all fit within a complete clearance budget.

The bearing handoff includes both native cartridge envelopes. Bearing selection still needs radial and axial loads, metal temperatures, speed and acceleration duty, life, stiffness, fits, preload, lubrication, drains, seals, and supplier applicability evidence. No bearing part number is selected.

Source: current performance study. The load JSON records the exact study hash and zero-based operating-point indices for each extreme. Gas temperatures are not bearing or rotor metal temperatures.

06Evidence boundary and sources

C5 finalizes the documented planning basis, generated requirements and SysML model. Native geometry and its R2 evidence remain unchanged. Hardware acceptance remains open. The source hashes were checked before generating this plan. Existing mesh measurements were not repeated.

Hardware verification needs objective evidence for the stated criterion and configuration. The verification record structure follows this principle. NASA Systems Engineering Handbook: Product Verification.

The bearing brief identifies required duty inputs before a part selection. Selection must address operating conditions and required performance. SKF Rolling Bearings catalogue.

These references guide the preparation. They do not qualify this engine or establish regulatory compliance. C5 source hashes and exact requirement mapping.
